meta.title: Gold Pays No Dividend, No Interest, Nothing. Investors Still Want It.
meta.hook: Gold pays no dividend. No interest. No cash flow at all.
meta.description: Gold's appeal as a 'safe haven' asset doesn't come from any income it generates — it generates none. It comes from being nobody else's liability: unlike a stock or a bond, owning gold doesn't depend on a company or government paying you back. That's why central banks and investors have leaned on it for centuries during currency instability and market stress. Educational content only, not financial advice.

scenes.narration: Gold pays no dividend. No interest. No cash flow at all.

visual.query: gold bars stacked close up macro shine
visual.visual_intent: Macro shot of stacked gold bars catching hard light, still and heavy, no motion graphics needed
visual.decision_reason: hook beat: the counterintuitive fact stated flat, hard cut

scenes.narration: So why do investors and entire central banks still hold billions of it?

visual.query: bank vault door heavy steel secure
visual.visual_intent: A heavy steel bank vault door slowly framed, weight and security implied

scenes.narration: Because a stock is a claim on a company's future profit. A bond is a promise from a borrower to pay you back. Both depend on someone else keeping their word.

visual.visual_intent: A financial contract or stock certificate on a desk, formal and paper-based, contrasts with the physical gold shot
visual.decision_reason: explains counterparty risk as the contrast concept, standard finance-education content

scenes.narration: Gold isn't a promise from anyone. It's just there, physically, regardless of what any government or company does.

visual.query: gold coins pile texture close up
visual.visual_intent: A pile of gold coins in raw texture, tactile and physical, camera pulling back slowly
visual.decision_reason: the payoff turn: physicality as the actual value proposition

scenes.narration: In nineteen seventy-one, the US even cut the dollar loose from gold entirely. Gold still didn't lose its appeal.

visual.query: archival vintage news footage 1970s black white president
visual.visual_intent: Archival-feel black and white footage of a 1970s presidential address, film grain, historical weight
visual.decision_reason: the 1971 end of dollar-gold convertibility (Nixon shock) is a well-corroborated, widely taught historical fact

scenes.narration: That's why it still holds its value when currencies wobble or markets panic. Not because it grows. Because it doesn't depend on anything else working.

visual.query: financial chart volatile market screen red green
visual.visual_intent: A volatile market chart swinging on screen, chaotic energy against the calm stillness of gold shots before
visual.decision_reason: visualizes market stress as the context where the safe-haven behavior shows up

scenes.narration: It's the one asset whose value doesn't rely on anyone else's balance sheet. That's the whole appeal.

visual.query: single gold bar spotlight dark background
visual.visual_intent: A single gold bar under a spotlight against total darkness, minimal and final
